title: Choose the visual world for camunda-eval
question: The roll dealt the analysis ledger. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Analysis Ledger
options.lineage: the accountant's columnar analysis pad and bound ledger
options.thesis: Every rule, version and line is an entry on a ruled pad: rows are commits, columns are the lines they belong to.
options.viewport: Work spaces: one ruled sheet. Account columns across the top (main, Release 1.3, 1.2, 1.1, each space), every commit a ruled row, its dot in its account's column; the picked row is ticked and the bottom band carries the one next action.
options.risk: Tips into heavy ERP if the ruling is drawn too dark or the type too small; it lives on generous rows and pale rules.

raised.raise: The pad's ruling is the layout armature: every row, column and gutter snaps to one ruled pitch, and the graph lanes are the pad's own columns.
Hierarchy by scale contrast: version numbers and table names set large like folio figures, labels tiny.
Destructive actions (close a line, remove a space) sit isolated by a ruled empty gutter, never beside a safe action.
Entries pack edge to edge in whole ruled cells; density comes from the grid, not from smaller type.

options.label: Transit Line Diagram
options.thesis: Release lines are coloured routes, versions are stations, landing is an interchange that carries a fix down the line to main.
options.viewport: Releases: the network diagram fills the stage, each line a coloured route; picking a station opens its tag action in the bottom band.
options.risk: Familiar: 'git graph as a metro map' is where most runs in this category land, and colour must then carry line identity.

options.label: Orienteering Course
options.lineage: ISOM orienteering map and control description sheet
options.thesis: Lines are the terrain; your work space's path to main rides over it in course purple, each step a numbered control.
options.viewport: Land: the graph as terrain, the landing chain drawn in purple control to control, the step list as the control description table.
options.case: Holds product clarity (your path over shared terrain is exactly landing) but analysts do not know orienteering.
options.risk: Without the map's own legibility, purple-on-terrain reads as decoration.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: Each screen is a junction sign: only the next decision, in black on yellow, everything else stays in the corridor.
options.viewport: A yellow band carries the one next action at the junction; the screen below is the corridor of lists and tables.
options.case: Holds 'one next action' perfectly; weaker on dense tables and the graph.
options.risk: Yellow everywhere collapses state colour; must stay reserved to the band.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.case: Poster grammar fights an all-day table tool.
options.kept: The grid as visible armature, now the ledger's ruling.

options.label: Variable Type Specimen
options.viewport: A giant glyph with axis sliders.
options.case: Nothing in the product is a typeface.

options.label: Convention Catalog
options.viewport: Hundreds of thumbnails in a numbered grid.
options.case: Thumbnail packing has nothing to show here.

options.label: Dark Console
options.case: You pinned a light theme; developer feel misses analysts.
options.kept: Destructive actions isolated by empty space.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean SaaS app: white, slate text, one blue accent, cards and a sidebar.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar of zones, page of cards, primary button in blue.
canonCard.risk: This is the generic dashboard you said would feel wrong.
